claim: Adam keeps two additional values per parameter, tripling the memory requirement relative to the parameters alone, which is the mechanism that makes a fully trainable 7B model cost three times its weight footprint before activations.
stance_target: The repo's claim that Adam state (84 GB for 7B) is the dominant memory term
scope_conditions: Adam-family adaptive optimizers with per-parameter second moments
quoted_support: For example, Adam (Kingma & Ba, 2015) keeps two additional values for each parameter, tripling the memory requirements.

claim: Adafactor replaces the full per-parameter second-moment matrix with per-row and per-column sums, reducing optimizer state from O(nm) to O(n+m) per weight matrix while reconstructing a low-rank approximation of the smoothed accumulator.
stance_target: Whether optimizer state can be made sublinear in parameter count, which would let a 7B model stay fully trainable on 64 GB cards
scope_conditions: Matrix-valued parameters; factored second-moment estimation with row and column sums
quoted_support: storing only the moving averages of these factors rather than the full matrix V yields considerable memory savings, requiring space proportional to n + m rather than nm.

claim: Adafactor matches the published Adam regime when training the Transformer on WMT14 English-German while using very little auxiliary optimizer storage.
stance_target: Whether swapping Adam for Adafactor would preserve the comparability of the repo's baseline runs
scope_conditions: Vaswani et al. Transformer, WMT14 English-German translation; factored second moment with update clipping and increasing decay rate
quoted_support: Combining these methods and dropping momentum, we achieve comparable results to the published Adam regime in training the Transformer model on the WMT 2014 English-German machine translation task, while using very little auxiliary storage in the optimizer.

claim: Adaptive methods can produce larger-than-desired updates when the second-moment decay rate is too slow; Adafactor fixes this with update clipping and a gradually increasing decay rate rather than a fixed beta2.
stance_target: The tuning burden of switching optimizer mid-programme
scope_conditions: Adaptive optimizers with exponential moving averages of squared gradients
quoted_support: Secondly, we show that adaptive methods can produce larger-than-desired updates when the decay rate of the second moment accumulator is too slow. We propose update clipping and a gradually increasing decay rate scheme as remedies.

claim: Adafactor drops momentum entirely and scales updates relative to the scale of the parameters themselves, so it is not a drop-in replacement for Adam in a comparability-controlled experiment.
stance_target: Treating an Adafactor run as directly comparable to an Adam run at the same hyperparameters
scope_conditions: Adafactor algorithm: beta1 fixed at 0, relative step size, parameter-scale-based update clipping
quoted_support: Finally, we propose scaling the parameter updates based on the scale of the parameters themselves.

claim: For a 7B model, Adafactor state is at most about 4 bytes per parameter (versus 8 for Adam m + v) and far less for large matrices, giving roughly 28 GB of optimizer state instead of 84 GB.
stance_target: Whether Adafactor alone is enough to fit 7B fully trainable in 64 GB without freezing Engram tables
scope_conditions: Arithmetic from the paper's O(n+m) state bound applied to 7B parameters; excludes activations; assumes Adafactor quality holds at 7B
quoted_support: Maintaining these per-parameter second-moment estimators requires memory equal to the number of parameters. For the case of neural network weight matrices, we propose maintaining only the per-row and per-column sums of these moving averages
